Question: Let \(S\) be the set of all numbers which are the sum of the squares of three consecutive integers. Then we can say that:

Choices.A: No member of \(S\) is divisible by \(2\)
Choices.B:
No member of \(S\) is divisible by \(3\) but
some member is divisible by \(11\)
Choices.C: No member of \(S\) is divisible by \(3\) or by \(5\)
Choices.D: No member of \(S\) is divisible by \(3\) or by \(7\)
